newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Detentions in Malaysia unfortunate says Australia.
newsitem.headline: Detentions in Malaysia unfortunate says Australia.

text.p: The detention of an Australian journalist and others by Malaysian police at a controversial conference on East Timor was unfortunate, Australian Deputy Prime Minister Tim Fischer said on Sunday.
"This is a very unfortunate incident," Fischer said of the dententions in a television interview.
He had been asked if the detentions would affect relations between Australia and Malaysia.
Fischer said he had spoken to Australian diplomats in Malaysia and to Foreign Minister Alexander Downer about the incident. Downer had asked for a report, he added.
"We have taken consular action overnight. I have been speaking to the Kuala Lumpur High Commissioner Bill Farmer and also to Mr Downer. Minister Downer has called for a full report," Fischer said.

On Saturday, Malaysian police detained 104 activists and two journalists, including Australian Broadcasting Corporation's Catherine McGrath, after a youth group allied to the Malaysian government broke up a conference in Kuala Lumpur on East Timor.
One of the activists detained was an Australian Roman Catholic bishop, the Rev. Hilton Deakin of Melbourne.
A Malaysian minister said earlier this week that the government did not want the conference to take place because it could harm bilateral ties with Indonesia.
Indonesia invaded East Timor in 1975 and now rules the territory in defiance of the United Nations.
Australia supports Indonesia's right to govern East Timor, but has called for a lower Indonesian military presence there.

Fischer said there may have been breaches of Malaysian immigration laws and he wanted more information on that. He also said the activists had attended the conference in full knowledge that Malaysian authorities had banned the meeting.

Meanwhile, the Australia-East Timor Association, which has campaigned for East Timorese independence, said on Sunday that Foreign Minister Downer should summon the Malaysian ambassador in Australia for an explanation of the incident.
"More urgently, Mr Downer should call for the immediate and unconditional release of all Malaysian detainees from the conference," association spokesman Jeff Lee said in a statement.

"Clearly, human rights have sunk to a new level in the region when Catholic bishops, academics and human rights activists are physically prevented from even discussing the important issue of East Timor," Lee said.
He said a protest over the detentions would be held at the Malaysian consulate in Sydney later on Sunday.
